ai.description: The Andaman Giant Gecko reaches 25 cm. It is grey-brown with irregular dark dorsal blotches and a pale underside. Key features include large, lidless eyes and prominent, broad adhesive toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gekko verreauxi* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of distinct, widely spaced, pale-edged dark blotches that do not form the continuous bands seen in other Indian *Gekko* species.
ai.habitat: The Andaman Giant Gecko inhabits tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically residing in the canopy or tree hollows at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Andaman Giant Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects and small vertebrates among the forest canopy and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gekko verreauxi* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Andaman Giant Gecko is endemic to the Andaman Islands in the Bay of Bengal, inhabiting lowland tropical forests across the archipelago.
